key_insight: Carefully selecting a subset of key/value tokens for attention in Visual Geometry Transformers cuts quadratic attention cost while keeping multi-view 3D reconstruction quality nearly intact.
problem_solved: Visual geometry transformers scale poorly because global attention grows quadratically with input token count, limiting efficiency and the ability to handle many views or high-resolution inputs.
method: Restrict the number of key/value tokens consulted by each query via a token-selection mechanism (e.g., learned scoring, confidence or clustering-based selection).
Insert the selection step into existing VGT pipelines with minimal architectural change so attention is computed over a compact set of tokens.
Optimize for compute/memory trade-offs to reduce FLOPs and memory footprint while preserving joint prediction performance for multiple 3D attributes.
impact: Makes multi-view 3D reconstruction models more scalable and deployable—enabling more views, higher resolutions, or resource-constrained deployment with little loss in accuracy. Practitioners can adopt token selection to reduce training/inference cost without redesigning the entire model.
visual_elements: Diagram comparing full global attention (dense KV connections) vs. sparse token-selected attention (few KV tokens per query).
Flowchart of the token selection pipeline: feature extraction → token scoring/selection → compact attention → 3D attribute prediction.
Chart showing compute/memory (FLOPs, GPU memory) vs. reconstruction quality for dense vs. token-selected models.
Before/after reconstruction visual: multi-view inputs and resulting 3D outputs to illustrate preserved quality.
paper_title: Good Token Hunting: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Token Selection for Visual Geometry Transformers
paper_authors: Shuhong Zheng, Michael Oechsle, Erik Sandström, Marie-Julie Rakotosaona, Federico Tombari
